learning_outcomes.text: The students are able to name and apply the fundamentals and methods as well as basic concepts of structural durability (stresses, amplitudes and mean values, load cycles, Wöhler line, Gassner line, influencing factors, ...) for carrying out lifetime verifications.
The students are able to independently plan and evaluate fatigue tests for determining Wöhler lines.
The students are able to name the different phases of material fatigue in the component and to identify and distinguish them based on fracture surface images.

The students are able to classify oscillating stresses with regard to their relevance to component fatigue (constant or variable amplitude, stochastic or deterministic) and to analyze them (counting methods).

The students are able to understand and estimate influencing factors on fatigue strength under constant and variable amplitude and to establish a connection to component behavior based on several interacting influences.
The students are able to understand the fundamentals of experimental and computational lifetime verification.
The students are able to elaborate simple computational lifetime verification using the nominal stress concept and to critically question the results obtained.

syllabus_topics: Component failure under cyclic loading / Fractography
Influencing factors on fatigue strength and statistical relationships
Computational lifetime estimation using the nominal stress concept
assessment_rules: The assessment is based on a 90-minute written exam. This exam accounts for 100% of the module grade.
